p263MovementTable.countingRule: Population = active buildable-envelope atoms whose `parcelNodeId` prefix is one of the six county fips, in the atoms store, with `outcome.kind = no-buildable-area` and NO `zero` proof. Bucket = the reason's class by `classifyEnvelopeAbsenceReason` (the SAME function the writer guard calls), plus one producer-attributed arm (see theMidWorkFinding). Every atom is in exactly one bucket; the run asserts `population == bucketSum` and exits non-zero otherwise. `alreadyComputedZero` and `notNoBuildableArea` are excluded from the population and reported separately so the apply cannot move them.
p263MovementTable.verdictOnTheTwoFiguresTheDispatchQuoted: The dispatch's 'mostly unzoned (208,868) or not onboarded (153,775)' is reproduced EXACTLY by the classifier: 208,868 and 153,775. That is not independent corroboration — the unzoned figure is one reason string repeated across five counties and the not-onboarded figure is one string repeated across four, so a classifier that catches them catches all of them. The informative result is the REMAINDER the dispatch did not name: 127,542 atoms, which CP1 predicted would be non-empty and which is not one cohort but 785 distinct reason strings.

theMidWorkFinding.what: The census's own classifier was the defect: it could only reach cohorts by ABSENCE CLASS, so 97,108 atoms — the largest single reason string in the population, `Tier-1 snapshot status no-buildable-area` (Williamson 81,554 + Travis 15,554) — fell into 'operator ruling needed' even though the ONE branch that writes that string is a branch THIS LANE FIXED. The dry run was therefore under-reporting what the change does: 362,643 atoms classified, 127,542 excused, when the producer-attributable cohort was sitting inside the excused bucket.
theMidWorkFinding.whyItMatters: The dispatch asks 'how many the change cannot classify'. An instrument that answers 'cannot classify' about a cohort whose producer is in this PR answers the wrong question, and the operator would have authorised an apply against a movement table that hid a quarter of it.
theMidWorkFinding.whatChanged: The producer now EXPORTS the retired string (`bake-from-tier1-snapshot.ts#LEGACY_TIER1_NO_BUILDABLE_AREA_REASON`) beside the honest one it writes today (`TIER1_STATUS_NOT_A_ZERO_REASON`), and the census imports it instead of keeping a private copy of the producer's literal. Movement becomes 208,868 -> not-applicable; 250,883 -> provisional-front-edge (153,775 absence class + 97,108 producer-attributed); 30,434 genuinely unclassifiable. The two arms stay separable in the artifact (`toPendingByTier1Status`).
theMidWorkFinding.whatGuardsIt: `bake-from-tier1-snapshot.test.ts` pins both directions: the branch reports provisional-front-edge with no `zero`, and the retired string stays distinguishable from the current one — if a future edit made them equal, the census would count the FIXED branch's own output as mislabelled and over-report the movement.
theMidWorkFinding.stateAtFiling: The amended instrument is committed and pushed (03c09ec); its re-run against the store is waiting on the heavy-scan lease, held by another lane (`integration-recover-48491`, heavy-scan, until 2026-09-17T21:51:39.519Z). The per-county numbers above are the 20:37:50Z measurement, which is the same query; the third arm's size is measured from that artifact's own reason rows (81,554 + 15,554).
theMidWorkFinding.theOtherInstrumentFinding: The P-260 registry instrument's first run summed 1,056,047 atoms against the store's 1,056,048 — an off-by-one that existed only because it matched cohorts by segment alone, so one county's spelling marked another county's tenant as already-counted (the hidden tenant is `breadth_null_elgin_tx`, 3,954 atoms). Keyed by (county, segment) the instrument's sum reconciles EXACTLY. Found because two numbers that should agree did not; fixed in ea1a59d.

theLedgerFinding.claim: P-260's Done includes 'every wired city in the six counties has a registry row whose cohort count matches the ledger'. The registry half is measured; the LEDGER HALF IS NOT MEASURABLE AS STATED.
theLedgerFinding.evidence: The ledger store is the factory store (`ep-round-base-au0jofwp...neon.tech`, database `neondb`); `public.parcel_record_cell` has exactly four columns — `place_key text, rail_key text, cell_state jsonb, updated_at timestamptz` (read from information_schema at 2026-09-17T20:53Z). There is NO city column on a cell, so no expression over `parcel_record_cell` alone can attribute a ledger row to a city; city attribution lives in the parcel identity (`public.parcel_record`), one join away. The instrument therefore REFUSES to guess an expression (`--ledger-city-field` is caller-owned) and reports the ledger column as UNMEASURED with that reason rather than as zero.
theLedgerFinding.whatWouldCloseIt: A ledger comparison keyed on parcels, not city names: join `parcel_record_cell` to `parcel_record` on `place_key`, take the city attribute from the factory's own schema, and compare per city against the atom cohort. That is a schema decision this lane does not own, so it is declared open rather than approximated.

LESSON: A movement census that classifies by REASON TEXT will excuse the cohort whose producer you fixed unless it also attributes by producer literal. The largest single reason string in a population is often one writer's status echo — look at the biggest unclassified row before reporting 'cannot classify'.

When two instruments' totals should agree and differ by one, the bug is usually in the key, not the data: matching on a non-unique segment across counties hid an atom and would have hidden more as county counts grow.

An 'absence' bucket that reproduces the dispatch's quoted figures EXACTLY is not corroboration: one reason string repeated across N counties classifies as N in whichever direction the classifier leans.
DEAD-END: Do not try to attribute a ledger cell to a city from `parcel_record_cell` — there is no city column (measured, not assumed). Any expression that appears to do it is inventing one.
